steps.title: Commercialisation
steps.body: The involvement of businesses and corporations in sport for financial gain. Sport is treated as a product to be marketed, sponsored and sold. Commercialisation has transformed modern sport from amateur participation into a multi-billion-pound global industry.

steps.title: The Golden Triangle
steps.body: The interdependent relationship between sport, media and sponsorship. Each element supports and depends on the other two, creating a cycle of mutual benefit that drives commercialisation.

steps.title: Balanced View
steps.body: Commercialisation has transformed sport, bringing enormous financial investment and global exposure. However, it has also changed the nature of sport, prioritising profit over tradition and creating inequalities between commercially attractive and unattractive sports. The challenge is maximising the benefits while managing the negative effects.

steps.title: PE Exam Tips — Commercialisation of Sport
steps.body: 1. For Commercialisation of Sport questions, use subject-specific terminology precisely 2. Support every point with specific evidence or examples 3. Show balanced analysis — consider different perspectives before reaching a conclusion 4. Link your understanding of Commercialisation of Sport to real-world contexts where possible 5. For longer answers, plan your response to address all parts of the question

steps.title: Exam tips
steps.body: Always explain the golden triangle as a three-way relationship, not just sport + money When discussing impacts, address specific stakeholder groups separately Give both positive AND negative impacts for balanced evaluation Use real examples of sponsorship deals to demonstrate knowledge Remember that social media is now a major part of the media landscape For evaluation questions, present both sides then give a reasoned conclusion
